name: Plant a tree properly
time: A day, then a season of care
blurb: Most young trees that fail were planted too deep, in a hole that was too small, and then never watered. Getting it right takes an extra twenty minutes and decades of payoff.
gear: A young bare-root or container tree
A spade, a stake and a tree tie
steps: Choose the right tree for the space at its mature size, not its size today, and check what is underground before digging.
Dig a hole two to three times as wide as the root ball but no deeper than it.
Plant at the same depth it grew before — the root flare must be visible at the surface. Burying it kills trees slowly.
Tease out circling roots from a container-grown tree, or they will strangle it.
Backfill with the soil you dug out, firm gently, and water thoroughly to settle it.
Stake low and loosely so the trunk can flex, mulch in a ring but not touching the trunk, and water deeply through the first two summers.
tips: Planting too deep is the single commonest cause of failure. Find the flare.
Mulch piled against the trunk causes rot. Leave a clear gap.
proof: A tree still thriving two years after you planted it, with visible new growth.
